outcomes: A visitor reads the reviewed support status of every classified package and protocol on one published page
A status change in the reviewed catalog reaches the published page without anyone editing the site
A reader can tell what each status commits to, and that an unlisted subject carries no promise at all
nonGoals: Classifying the deployed sites themselves, which the support protocol deliberately does not cover
Restating release planning, compatibility, or license-transition decisions that RELEASE.md and LICENSE.md own
Presenting feature maturity as if it were a support commitment

requirements.text: Every published support status is rendered from the workspace-root support catalog; the site holds no second list of statuses.
Only the three reviewed statuses are accepted and rendered; a catalog carrying any other status token fails the build instead of being displayed.

A catalog that is unreadable, carries a protocolVersion other than the exact integer 1, repeats a (kind, id) identity, or claims an experimental subject is default-on fails the build rather than publishing a partial page.
The independent non-default and no-parity claims are published for the subjects that carry them, and no claim is shown for a subject that omits it.
A documented surface the catalog does not classify renders no status badge, and the page states that an unlisted subject has no reviewed public support status.
The published page states that support status and feature maturity are different concepts and links to the feature-spec guide rather than merging the two vocabularies.
The published page is a pure function of the reviewed catalog, so repeated builds write identical bytes and entries keep a stable order.
The generated page exists before the docs tree is enumerated for static paths, so a cold build publishes the same page set as a warm one.
